landings.description: latent.gaba_harm_state_recurrence. Gives the SD-036 GABAergic decay regulator TEMPORAL authority over z_harm (SD-010) and z_harm_a (SD-011), which it did not have from its 2026-04-22 implementation until now. LatentStack.encode() produced both harm streams as PURE FEEDFORWARD encodes of the current observation, so the regulator's per-tick rescale was overwritten on the next tick and z_s(t+1) was not a function of z_s(t) at all -- the regulator degenerated to a one-step constant rescale, which every scale-free DV (including the registered falsifier's harm_norm_sustain_ratio) is exactly invariant to. z_beta was never affected (it already blends with prev_state), and that contrast is what localised the defect. Fix: a prev_state blend in encode(), z_s(t) = alpha_s*encode(obs_t) + (1-alpha_s)*z_s_decayed(t-1), composing with the regulator's rescale into a leaky integrator with pole (1-alpha_s)*exp(-tau_s*gaba_tone), so gaba_tone moves the trajectory SHAPE and not just its scale. The decay arithmetic stays in the regulator. Gated by REEConfig.use_gabaergic_decay (default False), mirrored onto config.latent by REEAgent.__init__. Contracts: tests/contracts/test_sd_036_gabaergic_decay.py C11-C16 -- the first SD-036 tests to step a real REEAgent through sense(), which is why the defect survived three months.

NOT mechanism-changing with the flag off -- the full latent trajectory is BIT-IDENTICAL to the pre-change substrate (max|diff| = 0.000e+00 on z_harm, z_harm_a and z_beta over a 60-step replay tape, measured against a detached worktree at the pre-change commit). Also not mechanism-changing for runs that enable the flag but never call sense(): those consume gaba_tone only as a scalar.

landings.mechanism_changing_note: TRUE when enabled -- it changes what E1's transition IS (action-conditioned rather than action-blind), which is the mechanism MECH-135 and INV-088 measure. But the master switch defaults False and no existing experiment sets it, so no prior run's substrate differs in any way: with the flag off no action_encoder is constructed, transition_rnn.input_size is unchanged, no construction-time RNG is consumed for the new path, and predict_long_horizon takes the pre-existing branch verbatim. Confirmed by re-running the V3-EXQ-954 driver --dry-run after the change: it reproduces the action-blindness signature unchanged (cr_ratio ~1e-07 at h=1). Blast radius on landed evidence is therefore nil until an experiment opts in.

candidate_stale.rationale: Two independent grounds. (1) The landing is default-OFF, so this run's substrate is byte-for-byte what it was. (2) It is an E2 training-horizon ablation and does not exercise E1's transition interface at all, so it is orthogonal to what changed.
candidate_stale.disposition: KEPT -- no de-weighting applied; KEEP needs no governance approval.

landings.candidate_stale_note: The two entries above are the ONLY experimental scoring entries for these claims (MECH-135: 16 scoring entries, 15 of them literature; INV-088: 7 scoring, 6 literature). No MARK and no REVALIDATE, so nothing here needed the governance approval Step 8.5(4) requires for de-weighting, and no index rebuild was needed to propagate a relabel. Separately: both claims already carry pending_retest_after_substrate: true (left unchanged by the V3-EXQ-954 disposition), so their retest is already owed and tracked -- that flag is what this landing makes ACTIONABLE, and the retest itself is /queue-experiment work for a later session.

landings.description: E1Config.output_proj_residual (default False): each rollout step in predict_long_horizon becomes `state_i + output_proj(lstm_out)` instead of `output_proj(lstm_out)`, in BOTH rollout branches (the ITEM 1 action-conditioned one and the legacy one), so forward() and predict_long_horizon() -- this entry's two substrate_paths -- are both covered. The form is copied from e2_fast.py's self_forward / world_forward (`z + delta(z, a)`) rather than invented; no scaling, gate, or extra module. The knob is INDEPENDENT of action_conditioned_transition on purpose: it parameterises the state recurrence, not the action channel, and the discrimination it exists to enable is an A/B ON the ITEM 1 ON arm. This is the design doc's own PRE-REGISTERED branch, fired because V3-EXQ-965 showed the ITEM 1 ON arm still crushed relative to the evaluator bar (cr_ratio(h=1) 25-37x short of 0.1). This landing is SUBSTRATE ONLY -- the A/B experiment is owed and no result is claimed. ITEM 2 (the multi-step / rollout-consistency objective) remains pending_implementation and is untouched here.
landings.mechanism_changing_note: TRUE when enabled -- it changes what E1's rollout read-out IS (a delta off the current state rather than an absolute next state), which sits inside the mechanism MECH-135 and INV-088 measure. But the flag defaults False and no existing experiment sets it, so no prior run's substrate differs: unlike action_encoder the change adds NO module and NO parameter in either setting, so construction-time RNG consumption is identical both ways. Confirmed by loading the pre-change e1_deep.py alongside the new one from the same seed: identical parameters and bit-identical rollouts (max abs diff 0.0) across three shapes -- legacy branch, ITEM 1 ON with a held action, and ITEM 1 ON with action_cond_unzero_self_slot=False. V3-EXQ-965 driver --dry-run re-run after the change: PASS, missing_action_calls=0. Blast radius on landed evidence is therefore nil until an experiment opts in.
